title: Why We Built Design Creativity Bench: Measuring What AI Coding Benchmarks Miss
gist: Kombai built Design Creativity Bench (DCB) to measure creative design decisions by AI models, evaluating 15 frontier models on 160 UI briefs (2,400 HTML interfaces) for originality, creative range and appropriateness. It finds models converge on similar designs (distinctiveness 0.592 between models vs 0.764 human-vs-model) and vary less across product contexts than humans (0.581 vs 0.902), while satisfying over 90% of requirements.

insights.claim: Kombai argues existing evaluations such as SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, VIBE Bench and Design Arena measure task completion and preference but miss whether AI-generated interfaces resemble designs models produce for many other products.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Design homogenization is an unmeasured quality gap that could differentiate AI frontend tools.

insights.claim: Anti-slop checklists that flag familiar colors, typography or card layouts only partly address repetition, since sameness also appears in information architecture and avoiding one style can push models toward another.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Surface-level prompt fixes are unlikely to solve AI design convergence.

insights.claim: DCB evaluated 15 frontier models on 80 UI tasks each adapted to two product domains, producing 160 briefs and 2,400 standalone HTML interfaces, compared against human reference designs.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Provides a scaled dataset for comparing frontier models on creative frontend work.
insights.locator: Giving models room to be creative

insights.claim: DCB scores originality versus other labs' models, creative range across paired product contexts, and appropriateness as the share of acceptance criteria satisfied, with similarity weighted 90% on information architecture and 10% on color system.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: A multi-axis metric that could shape how AI design tools are marketed and evaluated.

insights.claim: The learned similarity scorer agreed with pooled human choice 82.5% of the time on pairwise comparisons and achieved an AUC of 0.85 on a held-out judgment set.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Moderate validation means rankings should be treated as indicative, not definitive.

insights.claim: Average distinctiveness between models working from the same brief was 0.592 versus 0.764 between human and model designs, meaning model outputs resembled one another more than the human reference.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Frontier models are converging on homogeneous UI output, limiting differentiation for products built on them.

insights.claim: Average creative range across models was 0.581 versus 0.902 for the human reference, so models kept the same design approach even when product domain and content changed.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Human designers retain an edge in context-specific design, tempering expectations of full design automation.

insights.claim: Every model met over 90% of acceptance criteria, with Claude Opus 5.5 reaching 99.2% versus 98.0% for the human reference.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Functional UI generation is largely commoditized; creativity becomes the competitive frontier.

insights.claim: GPT-6 Astra had the highest originality at 0.646 but among the narrowest creative range at 0.472, and across the panel there was no statistically significant rank association between originality and range.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: A model can have a distinctive house style yet repeat itself, so single creativity scores mislead.

insights.claim: Kombai has not identified why models converge, listing training data, objectives, post-training and inference settings as possible causes, and results reflect default sampling without diversity-seeking prompts.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Leaves open whether convergence is fixable via prompting or tooling, an opportunity for design-focused AI vendors.
insights.quote: We have not identified why models converge.

insights.claim: The public release is a reproducibility subset of 300 HTML designs across 20 prompts and 15 models, whose scores should not be compared directly with the paper's full evaluation.
insights.speaker: Mukund Mohan
insights.so_what: Limits independent verification of the headline leaderboard.
